Every officer bears personal responsibility for the conduct of soldiers under their direct command.

Battle inoculation exposes officers to the sounds, confusion, and physical demands of combat in a controlled but realistic environment
The goal is not to eliminate fear but to ensure sound decision-making persists despite it
Repeated, progressively realistic exposure builds the confidence needed for real engagements.

Crisis management at the staff level requires rapid, disciplined decision-making even when the available information is incomplete or contradictory
Officers must resist the urge to wait for perfect information before acting on a developing situation
A timely, reasonable decision consistently outperforms a delayed, theoretically optimal one.
